messages:
mike: Heads-up: reproducing a perf regression tied to continuous-batching + KV reuse on long-context traces in staging. p95 token latency up ~2.3x after the cont-batcher reorder change.
anya: Ugh. Which workload/version?
mike: longctx-chat-64k, model v2.7. Kernel selection looks fine in isolation but when batches merge we see repeated KV fragment churn. Memory climbs over time (30m) instead of stabilizing.
dave: Any flamegraphs or perf samples?
mike: Pushed a short trace and a couple of samples to the thread. Main symptoms: head-of-line blocking on merged batches waiting for KV fragment reclamation; while waiting other requests hold onto slots -> cascading growth and eventual page thrash.
leah: Can you paste the perf snippet?
mike: ```
# perf top (sampled during the stall)
12.3% runtime::kv_fragment_merge
9.8% runtime::contbatch::wait_on_head
8.4% gpu_kernel::attention_v2
6.1% runtime::kv_reclaim_sync
5.2% scheduler::batch_coordinator
```
anya: That kv_reclaim_sync percent is suspicious. Should be async mostly. Did we accidentally make a sync path when merging?
mike: Exactly. Looking at the merge codepath, if a merged batch contains a mix of pinned+unpinned fragments we call reclaim() inline to normalize residency. On longctx workloads that causes blocking.
dave: How does kernel selection factor in?
mike: Kernel selection probes sequence-length distribution from per-batch histograms. When a merged batch inherits fragments from older requests, the observed seq_len distribution becomes bimodal. The kernel selector picks a general-purpose kernel less optimal for the hot path, increasing token compute and stalling the KV pipeline further.
leah: So two problems: blocking reclaim and suboptimal kernel choice after merge. Both amplify each other.
ninja: (infra-bot): deploy scheduled: staging/contbatch-fix-try-1 at 2024-09-12T15:40Z
anya: I ran a small experiment: forcing merged batches to prefer the newer fragment's seq_len for kernel selection reduced p95 by ~20% on a 5m run, but memory still drifted.
mike: Good signal. I also instrumented KV-fragment residency. The pattern: merge -> inline reclaim -> short-lived free -> immediate reallocation in next batch -> fragmentation increases (many small slabs) -> allocator overhead + page faults.
dave: Can you paste the allocator stats snippet?
mike: ```
kv_alloc: total_fragments=12456
fragment_sizes: median=4KB mean=12KB tail=256KB
slab_ops: alloc=312k free=308k reclaim_sync=12k
page_faults: minor=482 major=21
```
leah: Those reclaim_sync ops (12k) map to the reclaim() calls you mentioned. If we convert reclaim() to a deferred background sweep that marks fragments for GC, we could avoid the inline stall. But need to ensure we don't run out of residency.
anya: We could add a fast-path: when merge sees mixed pinned/unpinned fragments, attempt a try_mark_and_defer() that avoids immediate free if free-list > threshold. That plus kernel hint from newest fragment should help.
dave: Also consider adding a merge-aware kernel hint: pass preferred_seq_len=\"newest\" down to selector so it biases microkernel choice. If it fails, fallback to conservative kernel but don't block.
mike: I prototyped try_mark_and_defer. Local reproducer: longctx load with contbatch merge disabled vs enabled shows drift only when inline reclaim is active. With try_mark_and_defer: p95 improves and memory stabilizes for 20m runs.
leah: Any edge cases? Risk of memory overcommit if we defer too much. We need backpressure signal to trigger synchronous reclaim when free memory < X. Also telemetry to catch slow leak.
ninja: (infra-bot): note: added metric runtime.kv.defer_count and runtime.kv.sync_reclaim_count to staging metrics.
anya: Can we add a short timeout for deferred fragments (e.g., 5s) so background sweeper will collect them before long-term drift?
dave: Yeah. Implementation plan:
- short-term: land try_mark_and_defer + kernel hint (non-blocking) behind flag; add threshold/backpressure check + 5s ttl for deferred fragments.
- medium-term: revisit allocator fragmentation: introduce slab coalescer for small fragments to reduce tail fragmentation.
- long-term: contbatch merging policy: avoid merging batches with high residency heterogeneity (measured by frag variance).
leah: Tests: create a synthetic runner that emits bimodal seq_len mixes and validates no reclaim_sync in steady state for 30m. Add regression test to perf CI that runs for 2m with representative traces.
mike: I'll open a PR with the flag and the metric patches. Putting an engineering note in the PR about kernel-hint interaction so selector folks can review.
anya: I'll take allocator coalescer spike after this lands.
dave: I'll own perf CI test.
leah: Thanks — huge if this fixes the longctx memory growth. Please post PR and link the staging run.
mike: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4321 — tests & staging run attached. initial staging run shows p95 down ~30%, defer_count ~18k, sync_reclaim_count dropped from 12k->900.
leah: Nice. Can we also add a small dashboard tile: \"contbatch kv headblock\" that charts reclaim_sync_count + contbatch_merge_rate + p95_latency ?
ninja: (infra-bot): dashboard tile request created: #2345
anya: Great progress. Follow-ups: watch for slab tail growth, validate no quality regressions from kernel hint.
mike: Will keep thread updated. Thanks everyone.
